issue_context.title: Exception in Samsung SmartTV when the TV is off
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have an automation to do a whole range of things (including turning off a Samsung SmartTV). The problem is when calling "call service" with "media_player.turn_off" and the Samsung Smart TV, it'll trigger a _send_key("KEY_POWEROFF"), but when the TV is off already, the remote control instance isn't initialized and the _send_key will throw an exception in line 243 (bridge.py) as self._get_remote() is None 

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.8.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

samsungtv

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/samsungtv

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
just call media_player.turn_off service for a samsung tv that is already off...


service: media_player.turn_off
target:
  device_id: 0ada1861678abd31a5982fcc551fbd1d
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
I fixed this simply by catching the exception in _send_key (line 243 in bridge.py) as follows

def _send_key(self, key):
        """Send the key using legacy protocol."""
        try:
                self._get_remote().control(key)
        except:
                pass
```


### Additional information

_No response_
